questions.question: A private-type sender has prior odds H:L of 2 : 1. An observed signal is half as likely under H as under L. What are the posterior odds?
questions.explanation: Bayesian odds update: posterior odds = prior odds times likelihood ratio, so 2 × (1/2) = 1. Thus odds H:L become 1 : 1, corresponding to posterior P(H | s) = 1/2.
